content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I need assistance with a problem I can't solve myself. I'm new to PLCs and working with a [company_name] modular controller and an analog module, connecting two sensors. I've written the program in [product_name] V8.1 and can successfully measure temperature on the display. After setting up Ethernet communication and analog threshold triggers, I configured my network card interface. When I start [product_name] software to create an online monitoring screen for my sensors, I follow online guides and documentation, but the connection always disconnects from the PLC, showing error $140001 and ###### in the IO field. I'm getting frustrated—does anyone know what I'm missing or misunderstanding? Best regards, [user_name].

Do you have a standard [product_name] module or a specific FS04 version? To my knowledge, with the FS04 version, making a connection to [product_name] Runtime may not be possible. If you have the FS04 hardware, consider starting a support request.

Thanks for the quick response! I bought a starter kit with article number [article_no]. If I can't connect with [product_name] software, what alternative can I use to display a simple monitoring/HMI screen on my PC? // [user_name]
Once more—could you confirm which version of the [product_name] module you have: Standard or FS04?
I'll need to check in the morning since I'm not currently at the location and can't recall exactly what I purchased. Best regards, [user_name].

I'm not sure I understand. If you have a program for your [product_name] device and want to communicate with [product_name] software, you must first ensure you've selected the correct device type in your project settings.

In the [product_name] configuration, I selected 'Standard' when starting my project. My module has article number [article_no]. In [product_name] software, I chose a generic controller option because I couldn't find the specific [product_name] device.
All versions of the [product_name] series (FS01 to FS03 or FS04) share the same order numbers, including starter kits. You can find the FS number on the right side of the module.
Uploaded a mobile photo of the status window for reference.
If it’s FS 04, does this mean I can't use [product_name] software with it?

Is there an alternative way to create a simple SCADA/HMI screen on my PC with this controller, or do I need to purchase a different device? I just want to monitor my boiler in the basement as a beginner project, but it's seeming quite expensive. Best regards, [user_name]. Thank you for spending time to help me!

For easy monitoring, you can use the integrated web server provided by the controller. This web server offers a virtual display, similar to the actual module or operator device, even if it's not physically available. You can use message texts in the program that will be shown via the web server.

Thanks for your time, [user_name]. I know about the web server but was hoping for a more custom and visually appealing SCADA interface on my PC. I want to display eight Pt100 sensors. What other controller model would you suggest for this task, compatible with [product_name] software? Also, is there a feature in TIA Portal for PC-based SCADA, or is it limited to HMI screens? Regards, [user_name]. As mentioned, I'm new to PLCs—please bear with my questions.

As previously stated, to my knowledge the new FS04 hardware can't connect to [product_name] Runtime or [product_name] (TIA Portal) runtime. Your options are an HMI device or a third-party PC monitoring application.

If you want PC-based monitoring, you can use the [product_name] Access Tool, which is an Excel plug-in available at [url]. Note that this is not equivalent to full SCADA functionality. BR, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user is trying to set up online temperature monitoring using a [company_name] controller and corresponding analog module, aiming for SCADA/HMI visualization on a PC via [product_name] software. Despite following guides and documentation, the user runs into persistent disconnection errors and learns through forum discussion that their FS04 hardware likely doesn't support the intended communication, leading to confusion and frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: No specific expectations were expressed by the user.
